reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound: V has lower electronegativity than Mo, so partial substitution should reduce electronegativity differences and likely enhance dislocation mobility in a BCC solid solution, while prior work on V-containing alloys (AlNbTiV, NbHfTiV) supports good mechanical behavior.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with a well-defined falsification criterion (ductility increase <20% or strength drop >5%), though the exact processing window and optimal composition are left somewhat open.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis directly addresses the research question by proposing a specific, plausible intervention with a clear mechanism and test, making it highly useful for guiding experimental work on improving plasticity in this alloy system.
